content: In Galatians, what is the first fruit of the Spirit Paul lists?
explanation: Then joy and peace follow. “But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace” (Galatians 5:22, BSB)

content: In Galatians, which of these is a fruit of the Spirit?
explanation: The Spirit grows good character. “But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness” (Galatians 5:22, BSB)

content: In Galatians, what is the last fruit of the Spirit Paul lists?
explanation: It follows gentleness. “gentleness, and self-control. Against such things there is no law.” (Galatians 5:23, BSB)

content: In Galatians, against the fruit of the Spirit there is no what?
explanation: These are always good. “Against such things there is no law.” (Galatians 5:23, BSB)

content: In Galatians, the fruit of the Spirit comes from whom?
explanation: God grows it in us. “But the fruit of the Spirit is love” (Galatians 5:22, BSB)

content: In Galatians, if you walk by the Spirit, what will you not gratify?
explanation: The Spirit leads us. “So I say, walk by the Spirit, and you will not gratify the desires of the flesh.” (Galatians 5:16, BSB)

content: In Galatians, since we live by the Spirit, we should walk in step with whom?
explanation: Follow His lead daily. “Since we live by the Spirit, let us walk in step with the Spirit.” (Galatians 5:25, BSB)

content: In Galatians, Paul warns walkers in the Spirit not to become what?
explanation: Do not provoke or envy. “Let us not become conceited, provoking and envying one another.” (Galatians 5:26, BSB)

content: In Galatians, Paul tells believers to carry one another's what?
explanation: This fulfills the law of Christ. “Carry one another’s burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ.” (Galatians 6:2, BSB)

content: In Galatians, Paul says all believers are one in whom?
explanation: Neither Jew nor Greek. “for you are all one in Christ Jesus.” (Galatians 3:28, BSB)

content: In Galatians, Paul says do not grow weary in doing what?
explanation: We will reap a harvest. “Let us not grow weary in well-doing” (Galatians 6:9, BSB)

content: In Galatians, Paul says he no longer lives, but who lives in him?
explanation: He lives by faith. “I have been crucified with Christ, and I no longer live, but Christ lives in me.” (Galatians 2:20, BSB)

content: In Galatians, for what has Christ set us free?
explanation: Do not return to slavery. “It is for freedom that Christ has set us free.” (Galatians 5:1, BSB)

content: In Galatians, how should believers use their freedom?
explanation: Freedom is for love. “Rather, serve one another in love.” (Galatians 5:13, BSB)

content: In Galatians, the entire law is fulfilled in which single command?
explanation: Love sums it all up. “The entire law is fulfilled in a single decree: “Love your neighbor as yourself.”” (Galatians 5:14, BSB)

content: In Galatians, whatever a man sows, he will do what?
explanation: God is not mocked. “Whatever a man sows, he will reap in return.” (Galatians 6:7, BSB)

content: In Galatians, Paul says the righteous will live by what?
explanation: No one is justified by the law. “because, “The righteous will live by faith.”” (Galatians 3:11, BSB)

content: In Galatians, when the time had fully come, whom did God send?
explanation: Born of a woman, under the law. “But when the time had fully come, God sent His Son” (Galatians 4:4, BSB)

content: In Galatians, Paul will boast only in what?
explanation: Through it the world is crucified to him. “But as for me, may I never boast, except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ” (Galatians 6:14, BSB)

content: To which churches did Paul write the letter of Galatians?
explanation: Galatia was a region, not one city. “To the churches of Galatia” (Galatians 1:2, BSB)

content: In Galatians, how many days did Paul stay with Cephas in Jerusalem?
explanation: It was three years after his call. “and I stayed with him fifteen days.” (Galatians 1:18, BSB)

content: In Galatians, in which city did Paul oppose Cephas to his face?
explanation: Cephas stood condemned. “When Cephas came to Antioch, however, I opposed him to his face” (Galatians 2:11, BSB)

content: In Galatians, what did Paul say about the letters he wrote with his own hand?
explanation: He wrote the ending himself. “See what large letters I am using to write to you with my own hand!” (Galatians 6:11, BSB)

content: In Galatians, where did Paul go after his call, before returning to Damascus?
explanation: He did not go to Jerusalem first. “but I went into Arabia and later returned to Damascus.” (Galatians 1:17, BSB)

content: In Galatians, James, Cephas, and John were esteemed as what?
explanation: They gave Paul the right hand of fellowship. “James, Cephas, and John—those reputed to be pillars—gave me and Barnabas the right hand of fellowship” (Galatians 2:9, BSB)
